Started the runtime validation and production-readiness assessment of the Collateral Release V3 prototype in the TAM environment. The current work focuses on executing the enhanced process through controlled scenarios to verify that the redesigned routing, parallel specialist reviews, inclusive gateway synchronization, return-for-correction behavior, assignments, lifecycle states, and recovery paths operate correctly at runtime.

The assessment also includes validating Collection persistence, decision-history behavior, notification flow, PDF&#x2F;email processing, technical exception handling, retry behavior, and the remaining production-readiness gaps identified during the previous QA review. Runtime evidence is being collected to compare the working V3 implementation against the original process and confirm which improvements are fully validated versus which still require remediation before client or production adoption.
Weekly Calls

Completed the latest Snap Send Solve Screen development based on all screen-related requirements agreed during the client meeting. The OneCouncil request selection was simplified into a single OneCouncil Request dropdown using the populated DESCRIPTION value, while the Screen now resolves the corresponding Request Type, Category, and Subcategory internally so the integration payload can continue supplying the required backend values separately. Pasted text

The dynamic-question experience was also refined to provide a more cohesive presentation of question number, text, required&#x2F;conditional state, and answer controls while preserving sequence, mandatory validation, typed controls, selection options, and conditional-expression behavior. The implementation continues to dynamically load the applicable questions according to the selected OneCouncil request configuration. Pasted text

A new OneCouncil customer&#x2F;NAR search feature was developed to replace the previous large dropdown approach. The Screen now provides a keyword input, explicit Search action, and single-select results grid showing the customer information required for comparison and payload generation. Searches are executed only when requested, avoiding the need to preload the approximately 500,000-record Collection, and support matching against Display Name, Email, and Mobile. Running a new search refreshes the results and clears the previous selection, while the existing Create New Customer path remains available. Pasted text Pasted text

The Step 2 layout was additionally redesigned to keep the extracted SSS reporter information, NAR search controls, matching customer results, selected customer, and new-customer option visually closer together so Customer Service officers can compare records without repeatedly scrolling between sections. All requested Screen enhancements from the meeting have now been developed and are ready for client review and further integration testing.

Analyze the existing ProcessMaker login-page structure and prepare the detailed implementation plan for the requested CoS customization.

This work includes reviewing the active background assets and responsive behavior, confirming the recommended image dimensions and format, defining the Public Files upload process, and preparing SQL queries to retrieve, back up, update, validate, and restore the login-footer configuration.

The subtask also covers the comparison between direct database and API-based approaches, identification of unrelated database commands that must be excluded, and definition of the functional, responsive, accessibility, SAML authentication, rollback, and deployment validation requirements.

The work remains in progress while the imported process is being validated in the target environment, including runtime testing of the BPMN flow, screens, data sources, collection references, assignments, and notification behavior.
